claims.text: PostgreSQL full-text search splits text into words and normalises them (lowercasing), matches on those words and can rank matching rows; a language configuration such as english also reduces words to stems (keyboards -> keyboard).
claims.source_hint: PostgreSQL 17 docs: 12.1 Introduction; 12.3.3 Ranking Search Results; 12.6.2 Simple Dictionary; 12.6.6 Snowball Dictionary

claims.text: PostgreSQL can keep an index for full-text search that maps each word (lexeme) to the rows containing it, so a word search reads only matching rows instead of every row.
claims.source_hint: PostgreSQL 17 docs: 12.9 Preferred Index Types for Text Search (GIN is an inverted index); 64.4 GIN Indexes, Introduction

claims.text: An ordinary B-tree index cannot serve a LIKE pattern that starts with a wildcard (e.g. LIKE '%phím%'); the planner reads every row, visible in EXPLAIN as a scan of the whole table.
claims.source_hint: PostgreSQL 17 docs: 11.2 Index Types, B-Tree (LIKE only when the pattern is anchored to the start); ADR 0030 lines 20-22

claims.text: LIKE compares characters, so with PostgreSQL's default deterministic comparison 'a' does not equal 'à' and LIKE '%ban phim%' does not match 'Bàn phím cơ'; LIKE neither ranks nor strips diacritics.
claims.source_hint: PostgreSQL 17 docs: 9.7.1 LIKE; 24.2 Collation Support (deterministic collations); ADR 0030 lines 20-22

claims.text: unaccent is an optional module supplied with PostgreSQL, enabled in a database as an extension; it is a text search dictionary that removes diacritics. The lesson states no unaccent output for Vietnamese letters.
claims.source_hint: PostgreSQL 17 docs: Appendix F (Additional Supplied Modules) intro; F.46 unaccent; ADR 0030 lines 34-36

claims.text: ADR 0030 states that PostgreSQL has no text search configuration for Vietnamese and picks one that does not cut word endings; the lesson attributes this to the ADR ('as it notes').

ADR 0030 options: LIKE adds nothing but reads every row, no ranking, no diacritics stripped; PostgreSQL full-text search in Catalog, inverted index, no copy; a separate search tool, richer matching, own capacity, but a copy fed via the outbox that lags, needs rebuilding, one more service.

ADR 0030 decision: search in Catalog, owner of products; words built from the name on that row (lowercase, unaccent, non-stemming config); query normalised the same way; inverted index; optional product-list parameter via ICatalog, under catalog-reads, caller's shop only, ordered by match then id.
Not built at stage-4: ICatalog.ListAsync takes only limit, offset and maxPriceVnd; ADR 0030 line 8 notes search is not built and the list still filters only by maxPriceVnd.
claims.source_hint: DonHang.Catalog/ICatalog.cs @ stage-4 lines 9-11; ADR 0030 @ stage-4 lines 8-9

claims.text: Design review deep dive (step 4): same normalising both sides; 'Bàn phím cơ' (product 1 in db/seed.sql) becomes ban, phim, co; 'ban phim' becomes ban, phim and matches; a query with diacritics also matches; renaming changes the words in the same row, no copy to sync.

The design review risk table lists how a name with đ normalises as a separate check for the tester when search is built. đ (U+0111) is its own letter, with no Unicode decomposition into d plus a mark.
claims.source_hint: product-search-design-review.md @ stage-4 line 83; Unicode Character Database: U+0111 has no decomposition mapping

claims.text: Matching whole normalised words finds no product for a misspelt word and knows no synonyms; the design review accepts this until ADR 0030's revisit condition.
ADR 0030 revisit condition: complaints about misspellings or synonyms above 5% of search feedback in a month (assumed), or search load exceeding headroom even after moving to the replica.

The design review leaves caching results per search text open: no measurement of repeated searches yet; assumed most searches differ, so a cache would hit rarely and add a copy to clear on rename; owner: the Shop team.
claims.source_hint: docs/design/product-search-design-review.md @ stage-4 lines 74-75 and last row of the challenges table

claims.text: ADR 0026 gives a large shop a database of its own; a shop moved under it carries its searchable words with its product rows.
claims.source_hint: ADR 0030 @ stage-4 line 50; design review line 96; mapping-fitness-functions lesson (ADR 0026: database riêng cho cửa hàng lớn)

claims.text: Choosing full-text search inside the existing database is right when the data is small enough to share it, as estimated (a few thousand products per shop); a separate engine when matching needs or load exceed what the database can give; LIKE only for tiny tables with exact text.

Try it, applying the rule as ADR 0030 states it (whole words, lowercase, every diacritic stripped): CHUỘT matches only Chuột không dây; ban matches Bàn phím cơ and Đèn bàn LED; phi matches none (whole words, not prefixes).
claims.source_hint: db/seed.sql @ stage-4 lines 5-13; ADR 0030 lines 34-36; PostgreSQL 17 docs 12.3.2 (prefix match needs :*)

claims.text: catalog-reads is the existing concurrency limit on product reads: one limiter per process shared by every caller (20 running, 5 waiting at stage-4); search runs under it.
ADR 0030 consequences: search shares the database with order placement; load is held by catalog-reads, the per-shop cap of ADR 0016, and a replica when capacity-plan.md allows.
